 JUDGMENT

Initially this petition is filed by the petitioner U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act 1989 against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him, in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
But during pendency of the claim petition, petitioner was reported to be dead.

Hence, his legal representatives are come on record and by way of amendment have claimed compensation on account of death of deceased petitioner Venkateshaiah @ Venkatesh.
02.

The brief facts of case of the petitioners is that:-
That on 04.08,2019 at about 05.00 p.m the deceased was walking on the left side of Kuppemalla - Nelamangala Road, near Kambadakallu, Solur Hobli, Magadi Taluk,
Ramanagaram District, at that time the Honda Shine Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-52-Q-1107 ridden by its rider, rashly, recklessly and negligently (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 with high speed and dashed against the deceased.

Due to which the deceased Venkatesh fell down and sustained severe head injury and other injuries and after 2 years died in the hospital and was shifted to Government hospital,
Nelamangala, wherein after first aid he was shifted to NIMHANS hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein he was admitted as inpatient for about 10 days and has Venkateshaiah Allias Venkatesh vs Pavithra.

C.H on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41645557/
2 undergone surgery and was discharged with follow-up advice.
After the discharge was under regular follow-up treatment at Nelamangala.

His left leg was infected and breathing problem due to injuries sustained in the accident and was under continous medication and was bedridden and was admitted in K.C. General hospital for 15 days and inspite better treatment, he succumbed on 13.08.2021 due to non- recovery from the infection at the fractured site of left leg and head injury and have spent Rs.80,000/- towards obsequies and last rites and Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical treatment and other expenses and prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 49 years and was working as Coolie and also agriculturist and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.
Due to death of deceased, petitioners have lost sole bread earner of their family and have lost love and affection.
Petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioners (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 No.2 to 4 are daughter and son of deceased.

The accident is occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the offending Motor Cycle involved in the accident and in this regard the Kudur Police have registered a case against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the Owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed its written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent and hence, she was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the entire case of the petitioner and admits that this respondent has issued the policy in respect of the Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-52-Q-1107 and the liability if any is subject to terms conditions of the policy and provisions of M.V. Act and the rider of the insured vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same at the time of accident and the owner of the said vehicle knowingly entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having the valid and (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 effective driving licence and hence, there is violation of policy conditions by the owner.

The accident in question was not occurred on account of rash and negligent riding of the insured vehicle and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation, income of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and the compensation claimed is highly exorbitant and pray for dismiss the petition against respondent No.2 with costs.
05.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following Issues have been framed by this tribunal: -
ISSUES 01.
Whether the petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Venkateshaiah @ Venkatesh S/o late Hanumanthaiah?

3 02. Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Venkateshaiah @ Venkatesh S/o late Hanumanthaiah was died on 04.08.2019 at about 05.00 p.m, on Kuppemalla - Nelamangala Road, near Kambadakallu, Solur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagaram District, due to rash and negligent act of the riding of the Motor Cycle bearing registration No. (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 KA-52-Q-1107 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
04

. What Order or Award?
06.
In order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 and closed her side evidence.
The Manager Legal Claims of the respondent No.2 Insurance Company got examined as RW.1 and got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3 closed its side evidence.
07. I have heard the arguments advanced by the learned counsels for the petitioner and respondent No.2 and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 In the Negative  Issue No.3 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 As per final order  for the following:
 (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.2231/2020  REASONS 09. Issues No.1 and 2:- In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these two issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
10. The petitioners in order to prove their case, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the petition averments therein.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel she admits that her husband was died after 2 years of accident and they had not conducted Post mortem and admits that after the accident her husband was taken to K.C.General hospital and has discharged on 16.08.2019 and also admits that after recovery from the injury her husband was discharged from the hospital and they have not produced any follow-up records and also admits her husband had filed this petition.
11. On perusal of her evidence, it is very much clear that the petitioner was died after two years of the accident and there is no Charge sheet filed against accused/rider of the offending vehicle for causing death of petitioner due to rash and negligent act and (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 even Venkateshaiah Allias Venkatesh vs Pavithra.

C.H on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41645557/
4
there is no Post mortem report regarding the accidental death of deceased and no Inquest report regarding cause of death.
12. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioners have got marked 20 documents as Ex.P.1 to 20 on their behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Kudur Police against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle and causing accident and causing simple injuries to the petitioner.
Ex.P.2 is a copy of Complaint lodged against rider of the offending Motor Cycle.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Wound certificate of the petitioner which indicates that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P.4 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.5 is copy of IMV report which shows involvement of the offending Motor Cycle in the road traffic accident and the said Motor Cycle was also damaged in the accident.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Notice U/Sec.133 of IMV Act issued to the owner of the offending Motor Cycle.

Ex.P.7 is copy of Reply to notice wherein the owner of the offending Motor Cycle has stated that she is the owner of the offending vehicle and her husband was riding the Motor Cycle at the time of accident without having driving licence and the said vehicle had valid insurance and RC as on the date of accident.

Ex.P.8 is Charge Sheet which discloses (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against rider of the offending Motor Cycle for his rash and negligent riding and causing accident and causing injuries to the petitioner and it also appears that the rider of the offending Motor Cycle ride the Motor Cycle without driving licence and hence, invoked Sec.181 of IMV Act for not having driving licence.
Ex.P.9 is Discharge summary which indicates that petitioner was admitted to K.C. General hospital as inpatient from 05.08.2019 to 16.08.2019 for 12 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.10 is Emergency case record.
Ex.P.11 is Outpatient records.
Ex.P.12 is ER record and Ex.P.20 is X-ray.

13. On going through the above oral and documentary evidence produced by the petitioners, it appears that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 04.08,2019 at about 05.00 p.m, on Kuppemalla - Nelamangala Road, near Kambadakallu, Solur Hobli, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagaram District, due to rash and negligent act of riding of Honda Shine Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-52-Q-1107 by its rider.

But the petitioners have miserable failed to prove that deceased was died due to accidental injuries and there was a nexus between (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 accidental injury and death of deceased.

Further, Ex.P.15 to 19 are Aadhaar cards shows that petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioners No.2 and 3 are daughters and petitioner No.4 is son of deceased Venkateshaiah @ Venkatesh and are legal representatives of deceased.

Accordingly,
I answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative and Issue No.2 in the negative.
14. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of deceased Venkateshaiah @ Venkatesh who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

The petitioner No.1 in her evidence and deceased petitioner in his pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 49 years and working as Coolie and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and have lost earning member of their family and have spent Rs.80,000/- towards obsequies and last rites and Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical treatment and other expenses.

15. As discussed above, during pendency of this petition, petitioner who filed the petition for claiming compensation on account of accidental injuries was died on 13.08.2021 after 2 years of the Venkateshaiah Allias Venkatesh vs Pavithra.

C.H on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41645557/
5
accident
and Ex.P.13
Death certificate discloses the death of deceased and there is no evidence on record to show (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 that petitioner was died due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.15 to 19 are the Aadhaar card of the deceased petitioner and Aadhaar cards of the petitioners No.1 to 4 who are the wife and children of the deceased.
As per Ex.P.14 Medical bills of said deceased had incurred medical expenses of Rs.12,721/- only.

In this case petitioners have not examined the doctor who treated the deceased petitioner and no documents on record to show that the petitioner has died due to accidental injuries, no Post mortem was conducted and Post mortem report was produced.
No Police complaint was lodged and no Charge sheet was filed for proof of death of deceased due to rash and negligent riding of rider of offending Motor Cycle and also there is no Inquest report.
Further, there is no evidence on record for the proof of age, avocation and income of the deceased.

It is settled principles of law that the legal heirs of an injured person who dies during a pending claim petition are entitled to compensation for the injury, regardless of whether the cause of death is related to the injury.
This is because the right to claim compensation survives to the legal representatives of the injured person.

(SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 The compensation may includes,
01. Loss of income - This claims survives as part of the loss to the estate.
02. Medical expenses - This claims survives as part of the loss to the estate.
16.

Therefore, under the facts and circumstances of the case, the petitioners being the legal representatives of the deceased are entitled for compensation under the head of loss of estate and medical expenses only.

Accordingly, the petitioners are entitled for Rs.18,000 + 12,721/- =
Rs.30,721/-.
17. Accordingly I hold that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.30,721/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

18. Regarding liability:- On behalf of the respondent No.2 Insurance Company, its Manager Legal Claims is examined as RW.1 and in her chief-examination evidence she has reiterated the written statement averments therein.

During the course of cross-examination by the petitioners counsel she admits that offending Motor Cycle had a insurance policy as on the date of accident and also stated that the rider of the Motor Cycle had no driving licence and denied to the suggestion that the rider of the offending (SCCH-3) 14 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 Motor Cycle had driving licence as on the date of accident.
Apart from the oral evidence, on behalf of the Insurance Company, she has produced copy of Policy as per Ex.R.2 which shows as on the date of accident the policy was valid and is in force.
Though notice has been issued to the owner as per Ex.R.3 to produce driving licence of the rider, but no driving licence has been produced by the owner.
Further, as per Ex.P.7 Reply given by the owner stating that rider had no driving licence at all.
According to Ex.P.8 Charge sheet, Charge sheet has filed against rider of the offending Motor Cycle for riding the Motor Cycle without driving licence.
Therefore, it is very much clear that the rider had no driving licence as on the date of accident.
Hence, policy terms and conditions are violated by the owner and rider.
Therefore, pay and recovery order can be passed under the facts and circumstances of the case and hence, the respondent No.1 Venkateshaiah Allias Venkatesh vs Pavithra.

C.H on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41645557/
6 being the Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, as per Ex.R.2 since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.30,721/- with a liberty to (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 recover the same from the owner, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.3 partly in affirmative.
19. Issue No.4:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.30,721/- (Rupees Thirty thousand seven hundred and twenty one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released equally in favour of petitioners through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.

(SCCH-3) 16 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 Draw award accordingly.

However, as per Ex.R.2 since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall pay above said compensation amount of Rs.30,721/- with a liberty to (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.2231/2020 recover the same from the owner, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of filing of the petition till the date of deposit.

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.30,721/- (Rupees Thirty thousand seven hundred and twenty one only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment with a liberty to recover the same from the owner of the offending vehicle.

On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, since the award amount is meager one, entire award amount is ordered to be released equally in favour of petitioners through E-payment directly to their account by obtaining their bank account details.
